chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Abdillah al-Khazzaz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, for the Ka'bah there is a moment in every day in which forgiveness is granted to whoever circumambulates it, or whose heart inclines towards it, or whom an excuse prevents from reaching it.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for those who cannot physically visit the Ka'bah?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this narration from Al-Kafi underscores the Ka'bah as a focal point of divine mercy, extending the reward of pilgrimage beyond physical presence to include sincere spiritual longing (hann) and valid impediments. This concept reinforces the idea that the sanctity of the House of God transcends geographical constraints, offering a unique window for forgiveness tied to the orientation of the heart towards the Qibla.
